o: Comes from S2, S3 and S4

It is the main somatic nerve of the perineum.
It also supplies the external sphincters.
Leaves the pelvis above piriformis

It leaves below piriformis through the greater sciatic foramen.
It then hooks round the sacrospinous ligament.
Supplies the external anal sphincter through the pelvic splanchnic nerves

It supplies the sphincter through its inferior rectal branch.
The pelvic splanchnics are parasympathetic.
Enters the perineum through the obturator canal

It enters through the lesser sciatic foramen into the pudendal canal.
The canal lies on obturator internus fascia.
Has the deep ring medial to the inferior epigastric artery

The deep ring lies lateral to the inferior epigastric artery.
Direct hernias come through medial to it.
Has the ilioinguinal nerve entering through the deep ring

The ilioinguinal enters by piercing internal oblique, not through the deep ring.
It then leaves through the superficial ring.
Has the conjoint tendon as its anterior wall

The conjoint tendon reinforces the posterior wall medially.
The external oblique aponeurosis forms the anterior wall.
Has the genital branch of the genitofemoral nerve entering through the deep ring

The genital branch enters at the deep ring and runs in the spermatic cord.
It supplies cremaster.
Receives the greater splanchnic nerves

Greater splanchnics (T5–9) pierce the crura to reach the coeliac ganglia.
Their fibres relay there.
Receives vagal fibres

Vagal fibres pass through without relaying.
They relay in the walls of the organs.
Contains ganglia where sympathetic fibres relay

The coeliac ganglia are where preganglionic sympathetic fibres synapse.
Postganglionic fibres follow the arteries.
Carries pain from the foregut, referred to the epigastrium

Visceral afferents travel with the sympathetic fibres.
Foregut pain is felt in the epigastrium.
The superior hypogastric plexus lies in front of S3

It lies in front of L5 and the sacral promontory.
So "presacral nerve" is a misnomer: it is prelumbar. (Last's p. 365)
The inferior hypogastric plexus lies lateral to the rectum

It lies on the side wall of the pelvis lateral to the rectum.
It measures about 5 cm by 2 cm (Last's p. 399).
Parasympathetic fibres relay in the inferior hypogastric plexus

None of the parasympathetic fibres synapse in it.
They relay in ganglia in the organ walls (Last's p. 399).
Only about half of the sympathetic fibres synapse in the pelvic plexus

About half relay in the plexus; the rest have already relayed.
They relay in the lumbar or sacral sympathetic ganglia first (Last's p. 399).
Have the right kidney higher than the left

The right kidney is usually lower, pushed down by the liver.
The left kidney is about 1 cm higher.
Have the renal vein behind the renal artery at the hilum

From front to back: vein, artery, pelvis.
The vein is in front.
Refer pain to the T6–8 dermatomes

Renal pain is referred to T10–L1, loin to groin.
These match the kidney's sympathetic supply.
Have a left renal vein crossing in front of the aorta below the SMA

It crosses in front of the aorta just below the superior mesenteric artery.
It can be squeezed there (nutcracker).
The iliohypogastric nerve supplies the skin above the pubis

It supplies the suprapubic skin and part of the gluteal region.
It comes from L1.
The subcostal nerve is T11

The subcostal nerve is T12.
It runs below the twelfth rib.
The ilioinguinal nerve enters the inguinal canal through the deep ring

It pierces internal oblique and enters the canal from the side.
It leaves through the superficial ring.
The genitofemoral nerve pierces quadratus lumborum

It pierces the front of psoas.
The subcostal, iliohypogastric and ilioinguinal cross quadratus lumborum.
Enters the abdomen at T10

It enters through the aortic opening at T12.
The oesophageal opening is at T10.
Gives the superior mesenteric artery at L1

The SMA arises at L1, behind the neck of the pancreas.
The coeliac trunk arises at T12.
Divides at L2

It divides at L4, left of the midline.
L4 is at the level of the iliac crests.
Gives the inferior mesenteric artery at L3

The IMA arises at L3 behind the third part of the duodenum.
It supplies the hindgut.
Early appendicitis pain is felt around the umbilicus

Midgut pain is referred to the T10 area round the umbilicus.
It moves to the right iliac fossa when parietal peritoneum is involved.
Diaphragmatic irritation can cause shoulder-tip pain

The phrenic nerve (C3–5) shares segments with the shoulder skin (C4).
Blood under the diaphragm causes this.
Testicular pain can be felt round the umbilicus

The testis develops at T10 level and keeps its nerve supply.
Its pain can be referred there.
Foregut pain is felt in the epigastrium

Foregut pain is referred to the epigastrium, T5–T9.
Midgut is umbilical and hindgut suprapubic.
